nodes.name: cash_flow.py
nodes.summary: Builds a chronological cash-flow ledger from transactions: purchases are debits, redemptions and dividend payouts are credits, and switch-in/out legs are excluded as internal transfers.

nodes.name: distributor_comparison.py
nodes.summary: Compares one member's holdings of a single scheme across distributors (PRD-03 FR-11): groups folios by ARN code, runs the shared FIFO lot engine per group, values units at current NAV, and resolves distributor names via arn_lookup.
nodes.languageNotes: Reuses holdings.py's _LOT_CONSUMING_TYPES constant for the same-date purchase-before-redemption tiebreak so the two engines stay in lockstep by construction.

nodes.name: holdings.py
nodes.summary: The FIFO holdings engine: replays each folio's transactions as purchase lots with a same-date purchase-before-redemption tiebreak, merges folios per scheme, and values remaining units at the latest NAV to produce holding rows with absolute and day-change gains.
nodes.languageNotes: Orders same-date transactions with a SQL case() putting lot-consuming types last, because Transaction.id is a random uuid4 and an id-only tiebreak would nondeterministically under-consume lots.

nodes.name: _process_folio_lots
nodes.summary: Pure FIFO lot replay: purchases append lots, lot-consuming types drain them front-first, dividends leave units untouched; returns remaining units and invested cost.

nodes.name: compute_holdings

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Unifolio is a mutual fund portfolio tracking and wealth-management platform for the Indian market, built as a free-core alternative to Mprofit. The README itself is just a placeholder title, but CLAUDE.md is the real map: it defines the MVP scope (CAS import, phone+OTP onboarding, a main holdings dashboard, and an analytics dashboard), the non-negotiables (Decimal everywhere for money, no raw CAS PDF or PAN storage, test-driven development), and points to the full spec set in /Docs. Since the last tour, the CAS import feature has grown from a simple upload-and-parse flow into a full stateful lifecycle (CAS-IMPORT-UPDATE-PLAN.md) — every later step traces back to a decision already made in these documents.

tour.title: Backend Entry Point
tour.description: backend/app/main.py is where the FastAPI application comes to life: it builds the app instance, configures CORS so the Vite dev server can talk to it, and wires in the routers for each logical service. This single file is the backbone that ties Auth, Import, Dashboard, and Analytics together into one monolith deployment — and it now mounts five routers instead of four, since the CAS import feature grew a dedicated lifecycle router alongside the original one.

tour.title: The API Surface
tour.description: These five routers are what main.py mounts, and together they define every HTTP endpoint the frontend can call. auth.py handles phone+OTP login and session refresh; imports.py still exposes the original simple parse/confirm flow; cas_imports.py is new — it fronts the richer stateful import lifecycle covered in Step 7 (upload, password retry, CAMS statement requests, coverage-gap reporting, opening-balance entry); dashboard.py remains the largest surface; and analytics.py exposes per-member and household-aggregate SEBI-category/AMC allocation. Seeing all five together shows the project's real shape: one feature area now has two parallel entry points into the same underlying import machinery.

tour.title: Core Data Model
tour.description: Every service you'll see from here on reads and writes these five files. db/base.py defines the single SQLAlchemy DeclarativeBase every model inherits from; models/enums.py is the central vocabulary — transaction types, plan types, import lifecycle status, ARN status — referenced across the whole schema and now the single highest fan-in file in the codebase; user.py, folio.py, and transaction.py are the User/HouseholdMember, Folio, and Transaction tables the FIFO holdings engine and every dashboard view depend on. folio.py now also carries coverage-gap tracking fields, a preview of the lifecycle feature covered in Step 7. Understanding these five files first makes every service you read afterward make sense immediately.

tour.title: The Decimal Discipline
tour.description: CLAUDE.md calls this out as a repeated, explicit requirement: a float anywhere in the money path is a bug. decimal_utils.py is the small, cross-cutting helper that enforces it — fixed-precision quantization for units (3dp), amounts (2dp), and NAV, used by every model and service that touches money. It's a tiny file, but it's load-bearing: skip it and the FIFO engine in Step 9 would silently accumulate rounding errors.
tour.languageLesson: Python's float uses binary floating point, which cannot represent most decimal fractions exactly — 0.1 + 0.2 != 0.3. The Decimal type stores numbers in base-10, making it the only safe choice for money, units, and NAV values where cumulative rounding errors would compound into real financial discrepancies.

tour.title: CAS Import: Upload & Parsing
tour.description: This is the original path a user's mutual fund holdings take into the system, and it's still very much alive. parser.py wraps the casparser library to turn an uploaded CAS PDF into normalized investor/scheme/transaction data; enrich.py resolves each CAS scheme name to an AMFI code via mfapi.in, using exact and fuzzy matching; and service.py orchestrates the two-step parse/confirm flow that api/imports.py from Step 3 exposes, building a TTL'd in-memory preview before anything is persisted. models/imports.py is where a confirmed import lands as a row — and it no longer just records a snapshot, it now tracks a full lifecycle status, which is exactly what the next step builds on.

tour.title: CAS Import Lifecycle: State Machine, Attribution & Coverage Gaps
tour.description: This is the major addition since the last tour: a second, richer way for a CAS statement to enter the system, fronted by cas_imports.py from Step 3. lifecycle_service.py orchestrates it end-to-end — validating uploaded PDFs, buffering password-protected files in an in-memory TTL cache while the user retries a password, and committing parsed transactions once successful. Every status change moves through state_machine.py, a finite-state machine that rejects invalid transitions outright rather than trusting callers to check first. Two services extend the flow beyond plain upload: attribution.py matches a parsed statement's investor identity against the household roster (auto-match, mismatch confirmation, or unrecognized-member prompt) before any data is attached to the wrong person, and cams_portal.py offers an entirely different on-ramp — requesting a free statement directly from CAMS via a mailback portal link instead of uploading a PDF at all. Once transactions land, coverage_gap.py detects missing opening balances by checking each folio's transaction sequencing, and lets the user backfill the gap manually rather than showing a portfolio that silently understates history.
tour.languageLesson: A finite-state machine constrains an entity to a fixed set of named states with an explicit table of legal transitions. Modeling import status this way — rather than as a free-form string field — makes illegal states (e.g. jumping from 'uploaded' straight to 'confirmed' without parsing) a raised exception instead of a silent data-integrity bug.

tour.title: Auth & Session Security
tour.description: Phone+OTP is the entire authentication model — no passwords. otp.py handles OTP generation, hashing, issuance, and verification with attempt lockout and expiry; session.py creates and refreshes hashed-token sessions and provides get_current_session/get_current_user, which CLAUDE.md names as the app's real security boundary; and models/auth.py is where both OtpRequest and Session are persisted, storing only hashed values, never raw OTPs or tokens. Every dashboard route from Step 3 ultimately depends on get_current_user to know which household it's serving.

tour.title: The FIFO Holdings Engine
tour.description: This is the heart of the Main Dashboard. holdings.py replays each folio's transactions as purchase lots — a same-date purchase-before-redemption tiebreak keeps consumption deterministic. aggregate.py fans every dashboard view out across a user's household members with placeholder-aware handling for members with no data yet, and snapshots.py backfills monthly portfolio values by replaying those same FIFO lots and pricing them with cached NAV. All three build directly on the Transaction and Folio models from Step 4, and this same engine is reused directly by the analytics allocation service in Step 11.

tour.title: Dashboard View Services
tour.description: Beyond holdings, the dashboard exposes several derived views, each a small, focused service: allocation.py buckets current holdings into asset classes and AMCs for the Main Dashboard; sip.py detects an active SIP by checking for a recent PURCHASE_SIP transaction; cash_flow.py builds a chronological ledger of debits and credits, excluding internal switch transfers; distributor_comparison.py groups a scheme's folios by distributor ARN and reruns the FIFO engine per group; and nav.py is the on-demand NAV cache standing in for a future scheduled job, degrading gracefully to stale cache on outage. Each one reads the same holdings data from Step 9 through a different lens.

tour.title: Analytics: Category & AMC Allocation
tour.description: This is the standalone Analytics dashboard, built deliberately by reusing rather than duplicating what already exists: services/analytics/allocation.py calls into the same FIFO holdings engine from Step 9, batch-fetches each scheme's SEBI category, and aggregates current value into percentage-weighted SEBI-category and AMC buckets. schemas.py defines the Pydantic response shapes pairing those buckets with per-member aggregate status, and the routes on api/analytics.py from Step 3 expose per-member and household-aggregate allocation views. Where Step 10's dashboard/allocation.py answers 'what does one member's portfolio look like today', this service is the foundation for the broader cross-household analytics views still to come.

tour.title: The Database Schema
tour.description: The Database-Schema-Unifolio.md doc is the exact, final schema every model in Steps 4 and 8-10 was built against — including the reference-data-vs-user-data separation and the transactions/nav_history partitioning that CLAUDE.md insists must be preserved. 0001_initial_schema.py is where that original design landed via Alembic; 0003_cas_import_lifecycle_and_coverage_gaps.py is the migration that caught the schema up to Step 7's new machinery — adding error_code/error_message/source_tab/statement-date-range/expires_at to imports, coverage-gap tracking columns to folios, and a new opening_balance transaction type, with parallel SQLite/PostgreSQL dialect paths.
tour.languageLesson: Alembic migrations are versioned, ordered Python scripts with upgrade()/downgrade() functions, each capturing one incremental schema change. Branching migration logic by dialect (SQLite vs PostgreSQL) lets local development stay lightweight while production schema evolution still targets the real database engine.

tour.title: Frontend Entry Point & Auth Onboarding
tour.description: frontend/src/main.tsx is the React equivalent of Step 2's main.py: it mounts the root App component into the DOM inside React StrictMode, alongside apiClient.ts's shared base URL constant and ApiError class used across the whole SPA. auth/api.ts wraps every OTP-login and household-member-CRUD fetch call, attaching the bearer token from session storage — the client-side mirror of Step 8's session.py. AuthContext.tsx resumes a session from the stored token on mount, and FamilyImportFlow.tsx is the onboarding orchestrator that queues per-member CAS uploads sequentially — but it no longer drives the old ImportFlow.tsx directly. It now delegates each member's upload to TwoPathImportContainer.tsx, the tabbed chooser that lets a user request a CAMS statement, upload an existing PDF, or view import history, the frontend face of Step 7's lifecycle machinery.

tour.title: Frontend Dashboard UI & Coverage-Gap Resolution
tour.description: DashboardView.tsx is the main dashboard screen — it fetches holdings, allocation, and now coverage-gap data for either the family aggregate or a single household member, the same family/per-member duality Step 9's aggregate.py implements on the backend. dashboard/api.ts is its dedicated client: a shared authFetch wrapper with typed getters for the dashboard routes exposed back in Step 3. New since the last tour: CoverageGapBanner.tsx surfaces Step 7's coverage-gap detection directly on the dashboard — an alert banner that appears when a folio's transaction history is missing earlier purchases — and OpeningBalanceModal.tsx is the form it opens, letting a user record the missing opening balance without leaving the dashboard.

tour.title: Infrastructure & CI/CD
tour.description: docker-compose.yml defines the local Postgres 16 container used for functional-test parity with production — local development stays on SQLite, but this container lets tests run against real Postgres before anything touches AWS. ci.yml is the capstone: it runs the fast SQLite pytest suite, a separate Postgres-functional suite against that same container, and the frontend build/test pipeline on every push and pull request, enforcing test-driven development across the whole monorepo — including the new suites covering the import lifecycle state machine, attribution, coverage gaps, and CAMS portal requests from Step 7.
tour.languageLesson: docker-compose service definitions declare desired container state — image, ports, volumes, health checks — so the same Postgres version used in CI matches what a developer runs locally, eliminating 'works on my machine' schema drift.
